notes:
Refers to both the position itself and the person holding it. In Japanese companies, {管理職|かんりしょく} typically includes section chiefs and above. A key distinction is that {管理職|かんりしょく} employees are often exempt from overtime pay under Japanese labor law.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {管理職|かんりしょく}に{就|つ}く: to take a management position
- {管理職|かんりしょく}に{昇進|しょうしん}する: to be promoted to management
- {管理職|かんりしょく}{手当|てあて}: management allowance
- {女性|じょせい}{管理職|かんりしょく}: female manager
- {中間|ちゅうかん}{管理職|かんりしょく}: middle management

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {役職|やくしょく}: job title or official position — broader than {管理職|かんりしょく}, covering any titled position
- {上司|じょうし}: boss, superior — refers to the person above you, not the position itself

definitions.explanation: a managerial or supervisory position within an organization; a person who holds such a position

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{管理職|かんりしょく}だ。
examples.english: He is in a management position.

examples.japanese: {管理職|かんりしょく}に{昇進|しょうしん}した。
examples.english: I was promoted to a management position.

examples.japanese: {管理職|かんりしょく}には{残業|ざんぎょう}{手当|てあて}が{出|で}ないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In many cases, those in management positions do not receive overtime pay.

examples.japanese: {女性|じょせい}の{管理職|かんりしょく}を{増|ふ}やすことが{課題|かだい}になっている。
examples.english: Increasing the number of women in management positions has become an issue.
